training_plan.nutrition: Dinner: pasta + chicken + bread. Pre-mix warm sports drink. Bed early.

A.name: Lower Body Power + Core

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.note: Activates glutes pre-load — reduces knee valgus under fatigue at mile 20+

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walk
exercises.note: Hip abductor activation; prevents IT band syndrome in high-mileage blocks

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.note: Eccentric-focused. Achilles tendon health is critical at 100 mi/week

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.note: Primary running economy driver (Beattie 2017). 70–80% 1RM. Single-leg = sport-specific loading

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: Posterior chain strength. Reduces hamstring strain risk, improves stride power

exercises.name: Weighted Step-Up
exercises.note: Addresses L/R asymmetry. Hip drive pattern mirrors running propulsion

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.note: Max glute strength. Directly improves ground propulsion — critical at goal marathon pace

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.note: High-quality reps only. 6 wks improves RE 4.5% (Saunders 2006). Drop 20% in taper.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hop + Stick
exercises.note: Reactive strength + landing mechanics. Reduces overstriding injury risk

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.note: Anti-rotation core = reduced lateral sway = better economy at race pace

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.note: Lumbo-pelvic control under fatigue — what fails at mile 22

exercises.name: Side Plank + Hip Abduction
exercises.note: Glute med prevents Trendelenburg gait pattern in late marathon miles

A.rationale: Session A targets posterior chain and single-leg power — primary drivers of running economy. Heavy loading ≥70% 1RM over 6+ weeks produces neuromuscular adaptations improving RE by 3–8% without significant muscle mass gains.

B.name: Upper Body + Deep Core + Mobility

exercises.name: Pull-Up or Lat Pulldown
exercises.note: Arm swing power. Strong lats reduce upper body fatigue at mile 20+

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.note: Scapular stability. Prevents shoulder rounding under marathon fatigue

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.note: Rotator cuff health; counters forward head posture that develops late in races

exercises.name: Front Plank (ISO)
exercises.note: Trunk stiffness = better force transfer from glutes to ground

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.note: Adductor strength. Underrated injury prevention for high-mileage runners

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.note: Anterior core engagement critical for maintaining posture at goal marathon pace

exercises.name: Russian Twist (med ball)
exercises.note: Rotational core endurance

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
exercises.note: Hip capsule mobility. Reduces hip flexor strain from daily high mileage

exercises.name: Pigeon Pose
exercises.note: External hip rotation — critical for long run recovery

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.note: Thoracic rotation + hip flexor + hamstring — full-body compound mobility

exercises.name: Soleus Stretch (bent knee)
exercises.note: Targets Achilles insertion — most injury-prone site in marathon runners

B.rationale: Session B balances the posterior-chain work of A with upper body pulling, deep core stability, and critical mobility. Marathon arm mechanics reduce whole-body energy cost ~5% — upper body strength is the most commonly neglected element.

C.name: Explosive Lower + Foot/Ankle

exercises.name: Eccentric Calf Raise (4s down)
exercises.note: 4s eccentric, 1s up. Gold standard for Achilles tendinopathy prevention (Alfredson protocol)

exercises.name: Banded Dorsiflexion
exercises.note: Ankle ROM limits stride efficiency if restricted — especially in faster paces

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift (heavy)
exercises.note: Highest running economy impact per exercise. Heavy = neuromuscular, not hypertrophy. Sprint form cues.

exercises.name: Jump Squat (light load)
exercises.note: Rate of force development — slows at mile 20. Counteracts ground contact time increases.

exercises.name: Bounding
exercises.note: Horizontal power + ground contact time. 6 wks: 3–5% RE improvement

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
exercises.note: Gold standard for hamstring injury prevention. Eccentric strength at long muscle lengths.

exercises.name: Glute Ham Raise
exercises.note: Hip extension power at faster paces — key for a fast finishing kick

exercises.name: Med Ball Slam
exercises.note: Total body power + stress relief. Full reset for the CNS.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.note: Hip flexor strength for high knee lift — degrades at race mile 22+

C.rationale: Session C emphasizes explosive work and heavy deadlifts — the two interventions with strongest evidence for improving RE in well-trained runners. Reduce volume 40% in taper (Wks 9–11). Skip entirely in race weeks.
